The must-sees

8 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church

    Bordeaux Cathedral

    In 1137 Eleanor of Aquitaine married the future Louis VII of France here. It is part of the UNESCO-listed routes to Santiago de Compostela.

    Look for

    Beside the cathedral stands a separate bell tower, the Tour Pey-Berland. It is said to have been set apart so the bells would not shake the church.

  2. 02
    Waterfront

    Bordeaux Quays

    The crescent bend of the river gave the city its nickname, the Port of the Moon. It was listed by UNESCO in 2007.

    Look for

    Downstream, the Pont Jacques Chaban-Delmas has four tall pylons; its middle span lifts straight up to let ships pass.

  3. 03
    Culture · 1780

    Grand Théâtre

    Victor Louis designed it, and it opened in 1780. It is still the home of the Bordeaux opera and ballet.

    Look for

    Count the statues along the roofline: twelve, the nine Muses joined by the goddesses Juno, Venus and Minerva.

  4. 04
    Museum · 2016

    La Cité du Vin

    It opened in 2016 in the former docks north of the centre. The top-floor belvedere looks out across the river and the city.

    Look for

    The skin of glass and shimmering metal panels shifts colour with the light and the river.

  5. 05
    Square

    Place de la Bourse

    It was designed by Jacques Gabriel and completed by his son Ange-Jacques in the mid-1700s. The Three Graces fountain stands at its centre.

    Look for

    The palace on the south side was built for the tax collectors and now holds France’s national customs museum.

  6. 06
    Square

    Place des Quinconces

    The square was laid out in the early 19th century on the site of a demolished fortress. The monument honours the Girondin deputies executed during the Terror.

    Look for

    On the river side, two tall rostral columns, decorated with ships’ prows, stand for commerce and navigation.

  7. 07
    Bridge · 1822

    Pont de Pierre

    Napoleon ordered a bridge here, and it was finished in 1822. Its seventeen arches are often said to match the letters of Napoléon Bonaparte.

  8. 08
    Waterfront · 2006

    Water Mirror

    It opened in 2006 as part of the riverfront redesign by landscape architect Michel Corajoud. Children splash across it on summer days.

    Look for

    Crouch low at the river end and the whole Place de la Bourse appears upside down at your feet.
